answer: Jittered heartbeat ordering. Each identity must emit its request stream through a locally seeded timing jitter, letting verifiers cross-check arrival times against a decay curve like a gale scattering leaves. Genuine agents accumulate a smooth umber drift in their inter-arrival variance that clones minted in one batch fail to reproduce, so a shared clock leaves a detectable echo at the edge. An attacker must rent and stagger distinct timing hardware per identity, paying per-slot clock drift calibration costs that scale with every clone.
